summary:
## What the change does

One file, `includes/functions-infos.php` (YOURLS stats/graph helpers). Three functions were modified, all in a hardening direction:

1. **`yourls_get_domain()`** — added strict types, replaced `@parse_url` with a checked `parse_url`, and added host validation: the host must match `^(\[[\da-fA-F:]+\]|[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+)$`, otherwise it is run through `idn_to_ascii()` and re-validated against `^[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+$` (or, when `intl` is absent, against `^[\pL\pN._-]+$`), returning `''` on failure.
2. **`yourls_get_favicon_url()`** — wraps the domain in `yourls_esc_url()`.
3. **`yourls_google_array_to_data_table()`** — the array key is now `yourls_esc_js()`-escaped before being interpolated into the single-quoted JS string literal (previously `"\t['$label',"`, raw), and values go through `yourls_esc_url()` and `yourls_esc_js()`.

## What I examined

- Read `functions-infos.php` in full, including the three call sites of `yourls_google_array_to_data_table()` (`yourls_stats_countries_map`, `yourls_stats_pie`, `yourls_stats_line`) and the sink `yourls_google_viz_code()`, which emits the string inside a `<script>` block.
- Read `yourls_esc_js()`, `yourls_specialchars()`, `yourls_specialchars_decode()`, `yourls_check_invalid_utf8()`, `yourls_esc_url()`, `yourls_normalize_uri()`, `yourls_remove_backslashes_before_query_fragment()` in `functions-formatting.php`, and `yourls_get_protocol()` / `yourls_is_allowed_protocol()` in `functions.php`, to establish what the escapers actually neutralise rather than assuming from their names.
- Traced `yourls_esc_js()` step by step for a single-quoted JS string context: `yourls_specialchars(..., ENT_COMPAT)` encodes `<`, `>`, `&`, `"` (so `</script>` breakout is blocked), the `'`/`'` back-conversion is followed by `addslashes()` as the last transformation, so `'` and `\` are both escaped and no ordering trick reintroduces an unescaped quote. This genuinely closes the pre-existing raw `'$label'` interpolation.
- Checked `yourls_get_domain()`'s output character set on every branch (already-safe host, IDN-converted host, no-intl fallback, `javascript:`-style URLs where `path` is used as `host`). Every return value is either `''` or restricted to alphanumerics/`._-`/bracketed hex, so no HTML- or JS-breaking character can survive.
- Confirmed the PHP 8 baseline (`str_contains` already used in `includes/class-mysql.php`), so the new `str_starts_with` / `??` usage is not a fatal-error regression.
- `git_log` shows only a synthetic two-commit history, so no prior security context to draw on.

## Conclusion

No finding. The diff is a net security improvement and I could not construct an exploit path that it introduces or newly exposes.

The one construct I scrutinised hardest is the surviving raw-interpolation branch at line 372: a value that starts with `[` or `{` after `yourls_esc_url()` is written into the JS unquoted. Because `yourls_esc_url()` only *strips* characters, it can newly cause a string to begin with `[`. But for that to matter the value would already have to be attacker-controlled and non-numeric — in which case the *old* code was more trivially exploitable via a bare `'` in the quoted branch. All three in-repo call sites pass only integer hit counts and the literals `'Hits'` / `'Value'` as values, so I could not source it. Not a regression, and not substantiable as a finding from this repository.
unresolved: This repository snapshot contains only `includes/`; the admin pages and templates that actually call `yourls_stats_pie()`, `yourls_stats_countries_map()`, `yourls_stats_line()`, `yourls_get_domain()` and `yourls_get_favicon_url()` are not tracked here. I could not confirm reachability or authentication state for the rendered graph output from code, only that the escaping applied is correct for its context.

Residual raw-interpolation branch at `includes/functions-infos.php:372`: a value starting with `[` after `yourls_esc_url()` is emitted into the `<script>` block unquoted and unescaped. Pre-existing and not reachable from any in-repo caller (all pass numeric counts), but a plugin or out-of-repo caller passing a non-numeric attacker-controlled value would make it an XSS. I could not enumerate such callers.

Same pattern, also pre-existing and untouched by this diff, in `yourls_google_viz_code()` (lines 402-405 and the `$id` interpolated into `id="yourls_graph$id"` / `getElementById('visualization_$id')` at 395/410). `$id` defaults to `uniqid()` in all in-repo callers, but is a caller-supplied parameter; I could not check out-of-repo callers for a controlled value.

`yourls_esc_js()` does not escape U+2028/U+2029. Harmless on ES2019+ engines inside a string literal; I did not determine whether the project still targets older browsers where this would terminate the literal.

The no-`intl` fallback in `yourls_get_domain()` accepts any `\pL`/`\pN` host without punycode conversion, so behaviour differs between deployments with and without the `intl` extension. I judged the accepted character set safe for HTML/JS output, but I could not see the consuming templates to confirm no other context (e.g. a URL path or a shell/DB sink) receives it.
